name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite. Levers vs baseline (endogenous-rule era): AI cognitive labor payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5), low robot integration friction (robotIntegrationExponent 0.5, diffusion 0.30), and a datacenter power-spend ceiling 10x baseline (0.5% of GDP). ROBOT/DC CAPITAL RESCORE (November 2026): robot and chips+facility capex builds robot and datacenter capital stocks inside K and is added to general investment orders, competing for finance rather than for general capital's desired expansion. Before, it was carved out of that expansion and froze general capital at ~$967T from 2049 (GDP 2100 ~$1,204T). DC capex (default $15B per average GW, 15% annual replacement) rises from ~$0.3T in 2025 to ~$0.7T in 2030, ~$34T in 2050, ~$86T in 2075 and ~$197T in 2100; datacenter capital reaches ~$1,150T of a ~$5,400T capital stock. Energy WACC reaches ~13.9% in 2075 and ~14.1% in 2100, the return on capital ~26%. Outputs reach GDP ~$3,792T, a labor share ~4%, generation ~1.84M TWh, robots ~455/1000 workers, datacenters ~768k TWh, emissions ~140 Gt/yr and warming ~3.78C in 2100. Treat this highly path-dependent upper envelope as a stress test, not a forecast; DC capacity rationing and dedicated lease/debt service remain unmodeled.
